prompt:
A single compound was assayed by IC50 against a single protein target in two different assays, reported in the literature.

Compound SMILES: CCN(C)C(=O)Oc1cccc([C@H](C)N(C)C)c1
Target (ChEMBL): CHEMBL5763

Assay A:
  Description: Inhibition of equine serum BuChE using butyrylthiocholine iodide as substrate preincubated with enzyme for 20 mins followed by substrate addition and measured after 20 mins by Ellman's method
  Assay type: B
  ChEMBL confidence score: 9
  Organism: Equus caballus
  Tissue: Serum

Assay B:
  Description: Inhibition of equine serum BuChE using butyrylthiocholine as substrate incubated for 5 mins followed by substrate addition and measured after 5 mins by spectrophotometric based Ellman's method
  Assay type: B
  ChEMBL confidence score: 9
  Organism: Equus caballus
  Tissue: Serum

Will the two reported IC50 values agree closely (within 0.3 log units), or differ substantially (more than 1.0 log units)?

Respond with exactly this JSON and nothing else:
{"call": "COMMENSURABLE" | "NOT_COMMENSURABLE" | "INSUFFICIENT_INFO",
 "confidence": <float 0-1>,
 "error_class": "assay_method" | "buffer_conditions" | "construct_mutant" | "organism" | "readout_type" | "potency_range" | "none" | "other",
 "reason": "<one sentence>"}

"COMMENSURABLE" means you expect the two reported values to agree closely.
"NOT_COMMENSURABLE" means you expect them to differ substantially.
error_class is your primary reason for a NOT_COMMENSURABLE call, else "none".
raw: {"call": "NOT_COMMENSURABLE", "confidence": 0.55, "error_class": "assay_method", "reason": "The two assays use substantially different preincubation times (20 min vs 5 min) and measurement times (20 min vs 5 min), which for a pseudo-irreversible carbamate inhibitor like rivastigmine (a progressive inhibitor) can lead to significantly different apparent IC50 values due to time-dependent inhibition."}

parsed.reason: The two assays use substantially different preincubation times (20 min vs 5 min) and measurement times (20 min vs 5 min), which for a pseudo-irreversible carbamate inhibitor like rivastigmine (a progressive inhibitor) can lead to significantly different apparent IC50 values due to time-dependent inhibition.
